lead: Manchester plumbing deals with long cold winters, old mill-era housing and multi-family homes. PipeMend sends licensed local plumbers across Manchester.
risk: frozen pipes, aging pipes in mill-era homes and boiler and heating issues
risk_short: frozen pipes, old pipes and boilers
why: The North End, the West Side and Rimmon Heights have homes and tenements from the 1880s to the 1930s, built for mill workers. Many have galvanized supply lines, cast-iron stacks and old sewer laterals.
Long winters freeze pipes near exterior walls and on porches. Many homes use oil or gas boilers, so heating and plumbing overlap.
water: Manchester Water Works treats water from Lake Massabesic. It is soft.
tips: Keep the heat on in every unit through winter.
Have your boiler serviced before winter.
Know where each unit's shutoff is.
areas: PipeMend works in the North End, the West Side, Rimmon Heights, the Millyard, Bakersville, the South End and every other Manchester neighborhood.
permits: Plumbing permits come from the City of Manchester Planning and Community Development Department, and plumbers must be licensed by the New Hampshire Mechanical Safety and Licensing Board.

faq.q: Do Manchester homes need extra freeze protection?
faq.a: Yes. Older multi-family homes often have pipes in outside walls and unheated porches. Keep heat on in every unit, open cabinet doors in deep cold and insulate exposed pipes.
